method: Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Split the wholemeal burger bun and toast the cut faces in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Set it on a clean plate.
Mix the measured light mayonnaise, tomato ketchup and wholegrain mustard in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Slice the chicken breast horizontally into cutlets about 1.5cm thick so they cook evenly and fit the bun. After handling raw chicken breast, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the chicken cutlets over a medium heat for about 5–6 minutes on each side, lowering the heat if they brown too quickly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat and the juices are clear. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato in the toasted bun, add the cooked chicken cutlets and the cold finishing sauce, then close the bun and serve immediately.
